A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multi-draft speculative-sampling work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite renaming, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original OPT experiments on Dolly, XSum, and WMT18, including acceptance probabilities, block efficiency, token rates, and generation-quality scores.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds target-temperature and three-draft temperature sweeps.

M1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds an alternative truncated-LP procedure: selecting the top s tokens replaces full sorting, and pairs outside the optimized subset receive weights of 1/2 instead of deterministic ranked selection. The established two-stage method and original truncated-LP algorithm remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Dolly, XSum, WMT18, and the same synthetic token-distribution setting. Added temperature and draft-count experiments change model configurations within retained tasks, rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain SpecTr, SpecInfer, single-draft speculative decoding, and the theoretical optimum where applicable. The new sweeps use these existing comparators; relocated tables do not introduce or remove comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds a Dolly target-temperature sweep from 0.2 to 1.0 with drafts fixed at 1.0, plus a three-draft sweep with two temperatures fixed at 1.2 and 1.4. The acceptance-probability experiment changes its stated LP cutoff from s=7 in v1 Appendix H.1 to s=5 in v2 Section 5.2, while retaining its table values; this does not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 tests sensitivity to target temperature, and Appendix J.2/Figure 9 tests successive selection with three differently tempered drafts. The existing LP/alphabet-truncation sensitivity study is retained as v2 Table 1.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over four arbitrarily chosen seeds and retain the same use of error bars and plus/minus summaries. No new uncertainty definition, confidence interval, significance test, or repeated-run policy is introduced.

E6.justification: The corresponding identical-draft plots substantially revise throughput results: on Dolly at draft temperature 2.4, IS improvement changes from approximately 8% in v1 Figure 3 to 42% in v2 Figure 8, and SpecTr changes from approximately -16% to +10%. Block-efficiency bars and existing numerical tables retain their values. New Figures 4 and 9 add temperature-sweep results.

T1.justification: Theorem 4 expands from independent non-identical drafts to arbitrary jointly distributed drafts, substantially relaxing its sampling assumption. New Appendix D.1 develops the K=3, three-token case, while Appendix G adds complexity arguments and a claimed truncation guarantee for the new variant. Theorems 1-3 remain, and the general K>2 formula remains conjectural. v2 Equation (9) also corrects the weight index in v1 Equation (11).

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the two-stage decomposition, exact two-identical-draft acceptance characterization, importance-weighted heuristics, and OPT efficiency claims. Renaming canonical architecture to canonical decomposition and rephrasing the conclusion do not materially change these core claims.

C2.justification: Remark 1 explicitly broadens applicability to sampling without replacement. Appendix G adds a practical explanation that small s controls LP cost and concentrated top-p distributions keep vocabulary-related computation manageable. Existing explanations of modest top-k gains and draft-computation overhead are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds implementation-oriented cost breakdowns for sorting, selecting the top s tokens, and solving the truncated LP, and explicitly identifies the non-identical experiment's single-draft baseline temperature as 1.2. New sweeps document their temperature controls. OPT model sizes, A100 hardware, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works. A limited positioning change occurs in Remark 1, which explicitly relates the generalized decomposition to Miao et al.'s non-identical drafts and Jeon et al.'s sampling without replacement. The Dolly reference changes are bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: Section 5 is reorganized from identical/non-identical drafts into top-p/top-k sampling, exchanging substantial experimental material between the main text and appendices. Section 4 is rewritten with explanatory subheadings, and background and notation sections are added. Terminology changes from canonical architecture to canonical decomposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 4 and 9, notation Table 9, and background sampling pseudocode. Several figures, tables, and the truncated-LP algorithm move between the main text and appendices. The matched identical-draft throughput plot is redrawn with a revised vertical scale; the histogram figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The broader theorem, added sensitivity experiments, and background/complexity material improve completeness and accessibility. However, revised Figure 8 contradicts retained Appendix J.1 prose describing baseline slowdowns, and the new variant's Equation (196) sums over tokens excluded by its own selection weights. These substantive consistency problems make the net quality effect uncertain.
